sections.html:
Ross sits just north of Pittsburgh. Its McKnight Road corridor is full of shops, many owners are older, and the transfer tax is shared by the township and the North Hills School District. Paperwork for a sale goes through the Allegheny County Division of Real Estate and the township Building office.

The township wraps around West View Borough and touches McCandless, Hampton, Shaler, Franklin Park, Perry North and Brighton Heights. Areas like Perrysville, McKnight, Evergreen Hamlet and Glenshaw hold houses of very different ages. Say what era and lot you have when you list or ask for an offer, since buyers search on exactly those details.

Close to a quarter of residents are 65 or older, which means many houses have long-term owners. If that describes yours, get a repair estimate before you settle on a price.

sections.h2: Occupancy certificates and the Building office
sections.html:
Phone the Building office before you list. The department issues permits, reviews plans, runs inspections and writes Certificates of Occupancy under the state's Uniform Construction Code. No separate resale inspection is described for a transfer, so the call tells you if your address is the exception.

The Building Inspections number is 412-931-7048. The office is at 1000 Ross Municipal Drive and answers Monday through Friday, 8 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. Unpermitted work causes the most trouble, so deal with it before a buyer's inspector finds it.

  • Permits are filed online through iWorq.
  • Give 48 hours' notice for an inspection and include the permit number, address, inspection type, preferred date and an on-site contact.
  • Plumbing permits and inspections go through the Allegheny County Health Department. Electrical inspections use the township's third-party agency.
  • The township cannot certify flood zones. A parcel in a FEMA Special Flood Hazard Area carries added requirements, so look up your parcel on the FEMA map.

New projects now follow the 2021 International codes with state amendments, so a buyer's renovation plans get reviewed under the newer rules.

Realty transfer tax in Allegheny County lands between 2% and 5% of the sale price. The state takes 1%. A municipality and a school district divide whatever remains. The Division of Real Estate can tell you the exact township and North Hills School District shares for Ross, and the county also posts them on a local rate page.

  • The county takes the transfer tax when the deed is recorded, and it wants a check apart from the recording fees.
  • Attach a Statement of Value (REV-183) if the deed leaves out the consideration or claims an exemption.
  • A deed between relatives may qualify for an exemption, and the wording should show it, for instance that the transfer is familial and exempt.
  • For exemption questions, call the Department of Revenue at 717-783-8104.

Get the rates in hand before you weigh offers. The tax comes out of your proceeds unless the contract puts it on the buyer.

The county sets your assessed value. A challenge starts with the Board of Property Assessment Appeals and Review, and the owner or any taxing body with a stake in the parcel may file. Hearings take place by phone. You may go without a lawyer, though school districts and municipalities usually bring one.

If the outcome disappoints either side, the next stop is the Board of Viewers at the Court of Common Pleas. Only whoever filed can withdraw, and the county has a withdrawal form for it. Special appeals are open all year when the Office of Property Assessments issues a written determination in certain situations.

Taxing bodies can appeal too. A hearing notice about an appeal the school district or township filed against your home is optional to attend. Any buyer who hears about a pending appeal will ask, so raise it yourself during negotiations.

Ross and West View together make up the North Hills School District, with North Hills High School as its high school. The district name appears in nearly every listing search.

Stores and offices line McKnight Road, Perry Highway (U.S. Route 19) and Babcock Boulevard, so buyers near those roads often weigh traffic against convenience.

sections.h2: List or take a cash offer
sections.html:
A listing fits a house that shows well when you can sit through a lender's timeline. A cash offer fits a house that needs work, an estate sale, or a seller whose date outweighs the last few thousand dollars.

  • Line offers up by what you net after transfer tax, commission, repairs and unpaid taxes.
  • Get written answers on who pays the transfer tax and what happens if an inspection finds a defect.
  • Confirm the closing date and whether the buyer can close with no mortgage contingency.

A short folder saves days. Collect your deed, any permit numbers and inspection sign-offs, and notes on work done over the years. Add the township and school district tax bills if you have them, plus any hearing notice tied to an appeal.

If the house is in a flood hazard area, include the FEMA map page. Buyers and their lenders ask for it, and it is easier to hand over than to chase. For a vacant or estate property, note who holds authority to sign, since a title company will want that settled before it schedules recording.

1. Call 412-931-7048 and ask whether your address needs a certificate or any open-permit sign-off.
  2. Close out unpermitted work. File the permit through iWorq, then request the inspection 48 hours ahead.
  3. If the parcel is in a FEMA Special Flood Hazard Area, pull the map and tell buyers early.
  4. Ask the Division of Real Estate for the township and school district transfer tax shares, and decide in the contract who pays.
  5. See whether any taxing body has an appeal pending on the house, and disclose it.
  6. Have the closing agent record the deed with its own transfer tax check and a Statement of Value when one applies.

A cash buyer skips the lender wait. The township and county steps still belong to the seller, so put them on your calendar from the start. For an inherited or estate house, settle who signs the deed and whether the family exemption fits before a closing date is set. Keep every permit, inspection sign-off and rate quote in one folder where the title company and the buyer can reach them quickly.

faqs.q: Who issues Certificates of Occupancy in Ross Township?
faqs.a: The township Building department does, along with permits, plan review and inspections under the state's Uniform Construction Code. Its inspections line is 412-931-7048.

faqs.q: What is the transfer tax range in Allegheny County?
faqs.a: Between 2% and 5% of the price, with 1% going to the state and the rest to the municipality and school district. Ask the county for the Ross and North Hills School District shares.

faqs.q: Can I appeal my Ross assessment before selling?
faqs.a: Yes. You or any taxing body can file with the Board of Property Assessment Appeals and Review. Hiring a lawyer is optional, and the county posts the appeal and withdrawal forms on its Appeals page.

faqs.q: Is a house in a FEMA flood zone harder to sell in Ross?
faqs.a: It can be, since a Special Flood Hazard Area adds requirements. The township cannot certify flood zones, so check the FEMA map for your parcel and tell buyers early.

faqs.q: Which school district serves Ross Township?
faqs.a: The North Hills School District, which also covers West View Borough. Its high school is North Hills High School.
